papers.title_in_file: Quantum Software Engineering and Potential of Quantum Computing in Software Engineering Research: A Review
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Discussion (section 7), Threats to Validity, Conclusions; body sections on QML, optimization and QSE tools skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A literature review of quantum computing for software engineering tasks and of quantum software engineering tools.

assertions.value: The authors report that their review finds quantum machine learning and quantum optimization have substantial potential for classical software engineering tasks, and that this area is still limited.
quotes: Our study reveals that quantum machine learning (QML) and quantum optimization have substantial potential to address classical software engineering tasks, though this area is still limited.
assertions.certainty_reason: Review finding from the authors' own literature selection; not an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that current quantum software engineering tools and techniques lack robustness and maturity.
quotes: Current QSE tools and techniques lack robustness and maturity, indicating a need for more focus.
assertions.certainty_reason: Review conclusion about the state of tools.

assertions.value: The authors state the review did not consider unpublished papers, pre-print articles, technical papers or theses.
quotes: we did not consider unpublished papers, significantly pre-print articles, technical papers, and PhD or Master's theses.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 8 states the exclusion as a limitation of the study.

papers.title_in_file: Loss Behavior in Supervised Learning with Entangled States
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, theorem and lemma statements (section 4 skimmed), Discussion (section 6), Conclusion (section 8); experiment details not read
papers.what_it_is: Analytical and simulated study of how maximally entangled training samples affect loss variation and trainability of parameterized quantum circuits.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in their simplified theoretical setting, the possible improvement of the loss function value in a constrained neighborhood scales inversely with the dimension of the state space when maximally entangled training samples are used.
assertions.anchor: Section 6 Discussion, p.19 (Theorems 1 and 2 in section 4)
quotes: The possible improvement of the loss function value (Section 4.2) in a constrained neighborhood scales inversely with the dimension of the state space.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytical results (Lemma 1, Theorems 1 and 2) in the idealized Frobenius-norm model; reader did not re-derive them.
assertions.reader_inference: Holds only in the idealized model; the paper itself says transfer to PQCs is not immediate.

assertions.value: The authors report from simulated PQC training that non-maximally entangled states, even those of maximal Schmidt rank, might lead to a more favorable loss landscape structure than maximally entangled states.
quotes: NME states, even those of maximal Schmidt rank, might lead to a more favorable structure of the loss landscape than maximally entangled states.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from a selection of PQCs.

assertions.value: The authors state that the idealized analysis differs from real PQC training because a PQC generally cannot represent the full set of unitary operators and its exploration of reachable unitaries is not guaranteed to be uniform.
quotes: the exploration of the accessible subset of unitaries is not guaranteed to be uniform
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 6 states the gap between analytical model and implementation.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, experimental setup paragraph, Discussion (V), Conclusion (VI); result tables skimmed
papers.what_it_is: Simulated study adding adversarial training to quantum federated learning, evaluated on a small MNIST subset.

assertions.value: The authors report that partial adversarial training (for example 20% coverage in a 5-client system) boosts robustness by over 12% compared to baseline models in their MNIST experiments.
quotes: even partial adversarial training (e.g., 20% coverage in a 5-client system) can boost robustness by over 12% compared to baseline models
assertions.certainty_reason: Single empirical study on a small MNIST subset; figures are in tables.

assertions.value: The authors report that under high-intensity attacks accuracy collapses to near-zero levels across all configurations.
quotes: where accuracy collapses to near-zero levels across all configurations.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result in the paper's own runs (attack-strength threshold is given as a symbol not copied here).

assertions.value: The authors state the experiments use only the digits 0, 1, and 2 of MNIST, with amplitude encoding into a 6-qubit circuit.
quotes: In this study, we focus on a subset of the MNIST dataset containing only the digits 0, 1, and 2.
This enables amplitude encoding into a 6-qubit circuit for the QNN.
assertions.certainty_reason: Setup paragraph states the dataset subset and encoding.

papers.title_in_file: Applications of Hybrid Machine Learning Methods to Large Datasets: A Case Study
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section II start, Discussion (VI); sections III to V results not read in full
papers.what_it_is: Simulation of a single-qudit variational quantum circuit with a hybrid autoencoder replacing a deep neural network for QKD time-series classification.

assertions.value: The authors report that a qudit-based VQC with a hybrid autoencoder gives the same classification performance as a deep classical neural network on their time-series task while significantly reducing trainable parameters.
quotes: replacing a deep classical neural network with a thoughtfully designed Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) in an ML pipeline for multiclass classification of time-series data yields the same classification performance, while significantly reducing the number of trainable parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study on one QKD dataset, simulated.

assertions.value: The authors report that the number of weights in the VQC is approximately one-sixtieth of those in the NN, with comparable performance.
quotes: Although the number of weights in the VQC is approximately one-sixtieth of those in the NN, their performance, as quantified by several metrics, is shown to be comparable.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study on one QKD dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state the qudit VQC was simulated, not run on a physical system, so any training speedup is only potential.
quotes: if the qudit-based VQC were a physical system, rather than being simulated as in this work, its training could potentially be faster than that of a deep NN
assertions.certainty_reason: Discussion states the simulation scope.

assertions.value: The authors state the model elements merit further theoretical investigation and additional testing on larger datasets to draw more robust conclusions.
quotes: We believe that all these elements merit further theoretical investigation and additional testing on larger datasets to draw more robust conclusions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of the limit of the evidence.

papers.title_in_file: Nonparametric Learning Non-Gaussian Quantum States of Continuous Variable Systems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Theorem 1 statement, bound discussion, Simulation Study summary, Conclusions; supplemental material proofs not read
papers.what_it_is: A kernel-based nonparametric method (KQSE) for reconstructing continuous-variable quantum states from tomographic data.

assertions.value: The authors state that KQSE, a kernel quantum state estimator, reaches a near-optimal convergence rate in squared distance, with no Gaussianity assumption or prior information.
assertions.anchor: Conclusions and main text after Theorem 1
quotes: Our estimator achieves a near-optimal convergence rate in squared distance
we do not assume Gaussianity or use any prior information, only measurement data, reaching the same rate of convergence.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 (convergence of KQSE) in the main text; reader did not check the proof.

assertions.value: The authors report that KQSE consistently gives the lowest reconstruction errors on simulated and experimental data and outperforms MLE-based approaches under model mismatch and noise.
assertions.anchor: Simulation Study and experimental validation paragraph
quotes: KQSE consistently yields the lowest reconstruction errors for both simulated and experimental data, outperforming MLE-based approaches in the presence of model mismatch and noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own simulations and one experimental dataset; details in the Supplementary Material.

assertions.value: The authors state their trace distance upper bound is not tight in general and needs prior knowledge of the PDF class to be tightened.
assertions.anchor: Main text, trace distance bound discussion
quotes: The upper bound we derive is not tight in general and becomes formally infinite unless the total variation is either compactly supported or decays sufficiently fast at infinity
This implies that some prior knowledge about the PDF class is needed to obtain a tighter bound using our method.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state the limit directly.

papers.title_in_file: A Leap among Quantum Computing and Quantum Neural Networks: A Survey
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Other Surveys, Conclusions; technical review sections skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A survey of gate-model and adiabatic quantum computing and of quantum perceptron and quantum neural network implementations.

assertions.value: The authors state that, from their survey, quantum neural networks and algorithms in general are still far from proving decisive supremacy over classical ones, and that such a goal has too often been claimed.
quotes: it is clear that quantum neural networks and algorithms, in general, are still far from proving decisive supremacy over the classical ones.
Too often, such a goal has been claimed.
assertions.certainty_reason: Survey-level conclusion without a single study behind it.

assertions.value: The authors state the survey introduces basic quantum computing concepts and explains the technologies of the Gate Model and Adiabatic Quantum Computing paradigms.
quotes: we introduce basic concepts related to quantum computations, and then we explain the core functionalities of technologies that implement the Gate Model and Adiabatic Quantum Computing paradigms.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states the survey's scope.

assertions.value: The authors state the survey mainly reviews variational learning approaches: QAOA, VQE, quantum perceptrons and quantum neural networks.
quotes: we devote our work mainly to reviewing Variational Learning approaches which encompass Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms, Variational Quantum Eigensolver, Quantum Perceptrons, and Quantum Neural Networks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 2 states the focus.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Conclusion and Discussion (IV); methods and experiment sections skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A hybrid quantum-classical framework (IQFMs) chaining shallow quantum feature maps with classically trained augmentation weights.

assertions.value: The authors report that in numerical experiments on noisy quantum data the IQFMs framework outperforms quantum convolutional neural networks without optimizing variational quantum parameters.
quotes: In tasks involving noisy quantum data, numerical experiments show that the IQFMs framework outperforms quantum convolutional neural networks, without requiring the optimization of variational quantum parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own numerical experiments, simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that on a typical classical image classification benchmark a carefully designed IQFMs framework achieves performance comparable to that of classical neural networks.
quotes: Even for a typical classical image classification benchmark, a carefully designed IQFMs framework achieves performance comparable to that of classical neural networks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own numerical experiments.

assertions.value: The authors state that simple circuits that avoid exponential concentration are typically easy to train, and that machine learning models based on measurement expectations tend to be classically simulable.
quotes: Simple circuits that avoid exponential concentration of physical expectation values are typically easy to train, and that the functions of machine learning models based on measurement expectations tend to be classically simulable.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' discussion point, not tested in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: Bears on whether shallow-circuit QML can show advantage; the paper treats this as an open direction.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum computing with differentiable quantum transforms
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Conclusions; examples in section III skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A Xanadu paper formalizing differentiable quantum transforms and implementing them in PennyLane.

assertions.value: The authors define differentiable quantum transforms as metaprograms that manipulate quantum programs in a way that preserves their differentiability.
quotes: Such transforms are metaprograms capable of manipulating quantum programs in a way that preserves their differentiability.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition, abstract and section II A.

assertions.value: The authors illustrate the framework with examples in gradient computation, circuit compilation and error mitigation, implemented in PennyLane.
quotes: We highlight their potential with a set of relevant examples across quantum computing (gradient computation, circuit compilation, and error mitigation)
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states which applications are shown; examples illustrate, not benchmark.

assertions.value: The authors (Xanadu, the maker of PennyLane) state that making transforms differentiable, parametrized and optimizable opens up the possibility of improved quantum resource requirements.
quotes: In this framework, the transforms themselves are differentiable and can be parametrized and optimized, which opens up the possibility of improved quantum resource requirements across a spectrum of tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Vendor description of its own library; stated as a possibility, not measured.
